abstract: Non-coding regulatory variation is the major driver of human phenotypic diversity, yet maps of cis-regulatory elements (CREs) and their variability across developmental cell types remain limited. Here, we integrated single-nucleus chromatin accessibility data from 54 mid-gestation human prenatal cortical donors to generate a CRE atlas comprising 1,165,697 candidate CREs across 104,266 cortical nuclei. Chromatin-state annotation classified 1.5% of CREs as bivalent promoters, 0.3% as active promoters, 39.8% as active distal enhancers, 1.3% as CTCF-associated insulators but 57.1% remain unresolved. Overlap with an external enhancer assay dataset showed that many unresolved CREs, nevertheless, exhibit regulatory activity; thus, current chromatin signatures underestimate the functional regulatory landscape. Pseudo-bulk analysis across major cortical lineages revealed that the prenatal cortical regulome is dominated by lineage-restricted CREs, with only a small core shared across all lineages. Restricted CREs were enriched for unresolved elements, intermediate-sharing classes were enhancer-dominant, and broadly shared CREs showed the strongest promoter-proximal and bivalent contribution. Lineage-selective transcription factor (TF) sequence grammar analyses identified progenitor-associated homeodomain programs and neuronal basic helix-loop-helix signatures, together with representative candidate regulators such as SOX10, NFIA, EMX2, DLX1, ARX, and RFX3. Across donors, developmental time, and sex, prenatal cortical CREs segregated into a stable versus variable regulatory compartments. Broadly, recurrent and developmentally persistent CREs had greater activity, on average, and greater enrichment for promoter-associated states, whereas donor-restricted and temporally restricted CREs had lower activity and were enriched for unresolved and enhancer-like elements. Sex-biased CREs were rare but highly specific: female-biased CREs were predominantly X-linked, broadly shared, and developmentally persistent, whereas male-biased CREs were more numerous, less resolved, and more restricted across lineage and developmental contexts. Together, these results define the prenatal cortical regulatory landscape at single-cell resolution, revealing a small, stable, promoter-rich core and a larger variable, enhancer- and unresolved-rich compartment in which lineage diversification is driven primarily by selective deployment of distal regulatory elements.
